Anika: FYI hitting a weird failure in the sampleapp rerank flow when using the batching helper. 🤔
Anika: When I send a batch of 3 queries + 5 candidates, the node sample app returns a 400 complaining about 'vectors length mismatch' but python sample works.
Chris: Ugh, that sounds like the helper is reshaping or re-ordering payload fields between SDKs. Can you paste the request body that triggers it?
Anika: pasted below (redacted keys):
```json
{
  "model": "rerank-open-1",
  "queries": ["q1", "q2", "q3"],
  "candidates": ["c1", "c2", "c3", "c4", "c5"],
  "embeddings": {
    "queries": [[0.1,0.2,...],[...],[...]],
    "candidates": [[...],[...],[...],[...],[...]]
  }
}
```
Anika: Node helper sends `embeddings.candidates` as a flat array rather than array-of-arrays for some input shapes (looks like it flattens single-candidate lists), which the runtime rejects.
Maria: Is this the batching helper that tries to pack multiple small requests into a single call? I remember it uses a fastpath for 1-candidate cases.
Anika: Exactly. The bug surfaces when one request in the batch had only a single candidate; the helper normalized that candidate to a 1D vector instead of [ [vec] ].
Sam: That would explain the 'vectors length mismatch' error. Runtime expects candidates.length == candidate_embeddings.length and the flattening breaks that.
Chris: Could also be an auth/retry compounding issue: when the SDK retries after a 401 refresh, the helper repacks the partial batch differently leading to ordering mismatch. Any 401s in your logs?
Anika: Yes — I saw a token refresh early in the trace. Devex sample app retried the whole batch after refresh, and because of the fastpath the second attempt had altered shape.
Leo: Minimal repro suggestion: run the sampleapp with three requests where one request has single candidate; enable debug logs. I can add an integration test to guard this.
Anika: Here's a minimal curl that reproduces the runtime error (works in python SDK, fails when piped through node helper):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/rerank \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rerank-open-1","queries":["a"],"candidates":["only"],"embeddings":{"queries":[[0.12,0.34]],"candidates":[0.45,0.67]}}'
```
Anika: Notice candidates embedding is flat — that's the culprit.
Maria: Good catch. Chris, can we add a normalization pass in the helper that enforces nested arrays for all embedding lists?
Chris: Yep. I'll push a tiny sanitizer to the node helper that checks each embedding field and wraps scalars/flat arrays into array-of-arrays. Also add a unit test that simulates a token-refresh retry to ensure repacking is stable.
Sam: Also add a note in the sampleapp README about this gotcha and what the SDK does on retries. Might save users some debugging time.
Leo: I'll own the test + changelog. Assigning to @chris for the code fix.
devex-bot: Deploy preview build created: pr/5242 — includes node helper sanitizer and test. :rocket:
Anika: Awesome — thanks team. After the fix I can validate against our internal production-like workload and report back. :thumbsup:
Chris: If anyone has other sampleapp parity oddities (field names, envelope shapes), drop them here and we'll batch-fix through a small rectangular PR set rather than piecemeal.
Maria: Filing a ticket for SDK docs update and adding an e2e for batching+auth.
Anika: Will follow up with logs and a short gist of the failing trace later today.
